subject.title: Model configuration accepts unvalidated model names, enabling silent misconfiguration

question: Should unknown configured model refs be warning-only in config validate/doctor, hard validation errors, or handled only at startup/runtime when catalog authority is incomplete?
rationale: The source path is clear, but the permanent behavior affects custom providers, forward-compatible model names, provider-discovered catalogs, and upgrade safety, so maintainer product policy is required before a repair lane is safe.

options.title: Warning-first validation
options.body: Add catalog-backed warnings for unknown configured refs with wording that distinguishes trusted catalog absence from custom or forward-compatible setups, without failing config by default.

options.title: Strict validation
options.body: Reject unknown configured refs during config validation and require an explicit compatibility/escape contract for custom or future model ids.

options.title: Runtime-only handling
options.body: Keep config validation permissive and rely on startup/runtime errors plus fallback notices instead of adding a new config/doctor analyzer.

recommendation.title: Warning-first validation
recommendation.body: Add catalog-backed warnings for unknown configured refs with wording that distinguishes trusted catalog absence from custom or forward-compatible setups, without failing config by default.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal spans the configured-ref package, model catalog, and config validation direction, which are the decision surfaces for this issue.
